1.title: Troubleshooting Clusters, Nodes and Components
1.text: Welcome to Module twelve: Troubleshooting Clusters, Nodes and Components. It covers the exam area Troubleshooting. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, and every task was run on a real cluster, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do three things. Troubleshoot clusters and nodes. Troubleshoot cluster components. Practice with nine hands-on labs worth sixty-six points.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Troubleshooting (thirty percent). Practice in this module: nine labs, sixty-six points, about sixty-nine minutes. Exam format: performance-based tasks in a live terminal, scored on the final cluster state. Validated on: Kubernetes version one point thirty-seven point zero (kubeadm-style kind nodes.

1.title: First look at the cluster, continued
1.text: First look at the cluster. Decide which layer is broken before you touch anything. kube control says "connection refused" or hangs. Layer: A P I server, or your kube config. Where to look: kube config server address; A P I server container on the control plane node. kube control works, one node Not Ready. Layer: that node's kubelet or runtime. Where to look: S S H node; system control status kubelet container D; journal control dash u kubelet. kube control works, new Pods stay Pending with no node. Layer: scheduler (or cordoned or tainted nodes). Where to look: kube scheduler container; kube control get nodes. Deployment exists but no Replica Set or Pods. Layer: controller manager. Where to look: kube controller manager container. Pods run but a Service or D N S fails. Layer: networking. Where to look: Module thirteen.

1.title: The node: kubelet and container runtime
1.text: The node: kubelet and container runtime. Two systemd services keep a node Ready: kubelet and container D. Not Ready means the kubelet stopped reporting or cannot work. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study. Exam tip: For a Not Ready node, check the kubelet and the container runtime and read journal control dash u kubelet.

1.title: The node: kubelet and container runtime, continued
1.text: The node: kubelet and container runtime. kubelet stopped or disabled (Lab twelve point one). Evidence: inactive dead. Fix: system control enable the now flag kubelet. bad kubelet configuration (Lab twelve point two). Evidence: journal: "failed to load kubelet config" or strict decoding error naming the field. Fix: fix slash var slash lib slash kubelet slash config dot yaml, system control restart kubelet. runtime stopped (Lab twelve point seven). Evidence: kubelet is active, journal: runtime or C R I (Container Runtime Interface) errors; node Not Ready. Fix: system control enable the now flag container D. wrong certificate or kube config path. Evidence: journal: X five oh nine or "no such file". Fix: fix the path in slash E T C slash Kubernetes slash kubelet dot conf or the cert file.

1.title: The node: kubelet and container runtime, continued
1.text: The node: kubelet and container runtime. wrong A P I server address. Evidence: journal: connection refused to the address. Fix: fix server in slash E T C slash Kubernetes slash kubelet dot conf. C N I (Container Network Interface) missing. Evidence: node Not Ready, "network plugin not ready". Fix: install or fix the C N I ( slash E T C slash cni slash net dot d ). disk, memory or P I D pressure. Evidence: describe node Conditions. Fix: free space, evict, resize.

1.title: The node: kubelet and container runtime, continued
1.text: The node: kubelet and container runtime. The kubelet config file is slash var slash lib slash kubelet slash config dot yaml (static Pod path, C group driver, D N S); its service flags come from a systemd drop-in ( system control cat kubelet shows all files); its connection to the A P I server is slash E T C slash Kubernetes slash kubelet dot conf. system control cat kubelet is the fastest way to find which files are involved. A Not Ready node's Pods stay Running in the A P I for a while (a grace period) and are then evicted; do not wait: fix the node.

1.title: The control plane: static Pods and crictl
1.text: The control plane: static Pods and C R I C T L. In a kube A D M cluster the A P I server, scheduler, controller manager and E T C D are static Pods. Their manifests are in slash E T C slash Kubernetes slash manifests or. The kubelet restarts a component when its manifest changes, so fixing a component means editing its manifest on the control plane node. When the A P I server is down, kube control is useless, so use the node tools. Exam tip: Fix a control plane component by editing its manifest, and back the file up first.

1.title: The control plane: static Pods and crictl, continued
1.text: The control plane: static Pods and C R I C T L. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

1.title: The control plane: static Pods and crictl, continued
1.text: The control plane: static Pods and C R I C T L. Find the typo, correct it in the manifest (the kubelet restarts the component), and wait: the A P I server needs about thirty to sixty seconds. Do not copy the file out and back; edit in place. Keep a backup before editing: cp kube A P I server dot yaml slash tmp or.

1.title: The control plane: static Pods and crictl, continued
1.text: The control plane: static Pods and C R I C T L. kube A P I server (Labs twelve point three, twelve point four). Symptom: kube control refused or timeouts; container Exited or unready. Usual breakage in the manifest: wrong the E T C D servers flag port, wrong cert or key file name, wrong flag spelling, bad the service cluster ip range flag. kube scheduler (Lab twelve point five). Symptom: new Pods Pending, no node chosen, no events from the scheduler. Usual breakage in the manifest: wrong the kube config flag path, bad flag. kube controller manager (Lab twelve point six). Symptom: Deployments get no Replica Set or Pods; nodes do not recover; P V Cs unbound. Usual breakage in the manifest: wrong the root ca file flag, cert path, flag. E T C D. Symptom: A P I server cannot start, "etcdserver" errors. Usual breakage in the manifest: wrong data dir, wrong cert path, peer or client U R Ls. Do not "work around" (set node name by hand, create Pods directly): the task asks for the component to be repaired, and the check looks at the component.

1.title: Your own access: kubeconfig problems
1.text: Your own access: kube config problems. If only you cannot reach the cluster, check your kube config before the cluster (Lab twelve point eight). The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study. Exam tip: connection refused can come from a wrong server address in your kube config, not only from a dead A P I server.

1.title: Your own access: kubeconfig problems, continued
1.text: Your own access: kube config problems. The admin kube config on a control plane node is slash E T C slash Kubernetes slash admin dot conf. "connection refused" equals nothing listens at that address and port (wrong server or A P I server down); "Unauthorized" or "forbidden" equals credentials or R back; "X five oh nine: certificate signed by unknown authority" equals wrong C A data.

1.title: Not broken, just switched off
1.text: Not broken, just switched off. Scheduling Disabled in kube control get nodes means the node is cordoned. Pods may stay Pending when all nodes are cordoned or tainted (Lab twelve point nine). Fix: kube control uncordon node. A taint you did not expect ( kube control describe node grep Taints ) keeps Pods away; see Module six. Resource pressure shows in the node Conditions. Exam tip: A node that shows Scheduling Disabled is cordoned: run kube control uncordon.

1.title: Certificates (quick check)
1.text: Certificates (quick check). kube A D M certs check expiration lists expiry dates. An expired certificate gives X five oh nine errors in component logs and in kube control. Renewal is kube A D M certs renew all followed by restarting the control plane Pods (Module three).

2.title: A checklist for any "cluster is broken" task
2.text: A checklist for any "cluster is broken" task. Is the problem in kube control (kube config) or the cluster? k the kube config flag slash E T C slash Kubernetes slash admin dot conf get nodes on the control plane node. kube control get nodes, then kube control get pods dash A grep dash v Running. For a node: S S H, system control status, journal control dash u kubelet. For a component: C R I C T L ps dash a, C R I C T L logs, the manifest. Fix the root cause, wait, and verify with the original symptom ( kube control get nodes, create a test Pod).

2.title: Lab 12.1: kubelet stopped
2.text: Lab twelve point one: kubelet stopped. This task is worth seven points, and you should plan about six minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. Node C K A worker shows Not Ready. Find the cause and fix it so the node is Ready. The fix must survive a restart of the node (the kubelet service must be enabled and running). Hint: S S H C K A worker, then sudo dash i; look at system control and journal control. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 12.1: kubelet stopped, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run S S H C K A worker system control status kubelet the no pager flag head -five. Then S S H C K A worker system control enable the now flag kubelet. Then kube control wait the for flag set to condition Ready node slash C K A worker the timeout flag set to one hundred twenty seconds. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 12.2: kubelet config
2.text: Lab twelve point two: kubelet config. This task is worth eight points, and you should plan about eight minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. The node C K A worker went Not Ready after someone edited the kubelet configuration. Find the problem in the kubelet logs, fix the configuration file slash var slash lib slash kubelet slash config dot yaml on that node, and bring the node back to Ready. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 12.2: kubelet config, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run S S H C K A worker system control status kubelet the no pager flag head -eight. Then S S H C K A worker journal control dash u kubelet the no pager flag grep dash i dash E yaml failed error tail -three. Then S S H C K A worker sed dash i or ^broken slash d slash var slash lib slash kubelet slash config dot yaml system control restart kubelet. Then kube control wait the for flag set to condition Ready node slash C K A worker the timeout flag set to one hundred eighty seconds. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 12.3: apiserver etcd flag
2.text: Lab twelve point three: A P I server E T C D flag. This task is worth nine points, and you should plan about ten minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. kube control commands fail or time out: the A P I server is not healthy. Connect to the control plane node C K A control plane, find the cause (container logs with C R I C T L, the static Pod manifest) and fix it. When done, kube control get nodes must work again. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 12.3: apiserver etcd flag, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run S S H C K A control plane C R I C T L ps dash a the name flag kube A P I server. Then S S H C K A control plane C R I C T L logs C R I C T L ps dash a the name flag kube A P I server dash q, and so on. Then S S H C K A control plane grep E T C D servers slash E T C slash Kubernetes slash manifests slash kube A P I server dot yaml. Then S S H C K A control plane sed dash i s the E T C D servers flag set to H T T P S colon slash slash one hundred twenty-seven dot zero, and so on. Then S S H C K A control plane system control restart kubelet resets the crash loop back off of the static Pod. Then until kube control get the raw flag slash readyz slash dev slash null two one do sleep two done. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 12.4: apiserver cert path
2.text: Lab twelve point four: A P I server cert path. This task is worth nine points, and you should plan about ten minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. kube control reports "connection refused": the A P I server container does not even start. On the control plane node C K A control plane, find out why (look at the container list with C R I C T L ps dash a and its logs) and repair the problem. When done, kube control get nodes must work. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 12.4: apiserver cert path, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run S S H C K A control plane C R I C T L ps dash a the name flag kube A P I server. Then S S H C K A control plane C R I C T L logs C R I C T L ps dash a the name flag kube A P I server dash q, and so on. Then S S H C K A control plane sed dash i s A P I server dot crt dot bak A P I server dot crt slash E T C slash Kubernetes slash manifests, and so on. Then S S H C K A control plane system control restart kubelet resets the crash loop back off of the static Pod. Then until kube control get the raw flag slash readyz slash dev slash null two one do sleep two done. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 12.5: scheduler broken
2.text: Lab twelve point five: scheduler broken. This task is worth eight points, and you should plan about nine minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. New Pods in the namespace sched one stay Pending with no node assigned (the Deployment probe app has two replicas). Existing workloads are fine. Find the faulty control plane component on C K A control plane and repair it so that both Pods are scheduled and become Ready. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 12.5: scheduler broken, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run S S H C K A control plane C R I C T L ps dash a the name flag kube scheduler. Then S S H C K A control plane C R I C T L logs C R I C T L ps dash a the name flag kube scheduler dash q head -one two, and so on. Then S S H C K A control plane sed dash i s scheduler dot cnf scheduler dot conf slash E T C slash Kubernetes slash manifests slash kube scheduler dot yaml. Then S S H C K A control plane system control restart kubelet resets the crash loop back off of the static Pod. Then kube control dash n sched one rollout status deployment probe app the timeout flag set to one hundred eighty seconds. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

3.title: Lab 12.6: controller manager broken
3.text: Lab twelve point six: controller manager broken. This task is worth eight points, and you should plan about nine minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. In the namespace cm one, the Deployment counter (two replicas) was created but no Pods appear and kube control get rs shows nothing. Find the faulty control plane component on C K A control plane and repair it so that both Pods run. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

3.title: Lab 12.6: controller manager broken, Solution
3.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run S S H C K A control plane C R I C T L ps dash a the name flag kube controller manager. Then S S H C K A control plane C R I C T L logs C R I C T L ps dash a the name flag kube controller manager dash q head -one, and so on. Then S S H C K A control plane sed dash i s ca dot crtx ca dot crt slash E T C slash Kubernetes slash manifests slash kube controller manager dot yaml. Then S S H C K A control plane system control restart kubelet resets the crash loop back off of the static Pod. Then kube control dash n cm one rollout status deployment counter the timeout flag set to one hundred eighty seconds. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

3.title: Lab 12.7: containerd stopped
3.text: Lab twelve point seven: container D stopped. This task is worth seven points, and you should plan about seven minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. The node C K A worker two is Not Ready; the kubelet is running but cannot talk to the container runtime. Fix the node so it is Ready again, and make sure the runtime service is enabled and running. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

3.title: Lab 12.7: containerd stopped, Solution
3.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run S S H C K A worker two system control is active kubelet system control is active container D. Then S S H C K A worker two journal control dash u kubelet the no pager flag tail -three. Then S S H C K A worker two system control enable the now flag container D. Then kube control wait the for flag set to condition Ready node slash C K A worker two the timeout flag set to one hundred eighty seconds. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

3.title: Lab 12.8: kubeconfig wrong server
3.text: Lab twelve point eight: kube config wrong server. This task is worth five points, and you should plan about five minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. The file about slash answers slash broken dot kube config is a copy of a working kube config, but kube control the kube config flag about slash answers slash broken dot kube config get nodes fails with a connection error. Fix the file (use kube control config commands; keep the cluster, user and context names) so that the command works again. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

3.title: Lab 12.8: kubeconfig wrong server, Solution
3.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control the kube config flag about slash answers slash broken dot kube config get nodes two one then pipe to tail -two. Then good kube control config view the minify flag dash o json path dot clusters zero dot cluster dot server. Then kube control config set cluster kind C K A the server flag set to good the kube config flag about slash answers slash broken dot kube config. Then kube control the kube config flag about slash answers slash broken dot kube config get nodes. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

3.title: Lab 12.9: cordoned nodes
3.text: Lab twelve point nine: cordoned nodes. This task is worth five points, and you should plan about five minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. In the namespace cord, the Deployment queue (two replicas) has Pods that stay Pending. The Pods have no resource problems. Find the cause and fix the cluster so that both Pods run (do not change the Deployment). Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

3.title: Lab 12.9: cordoned nodes, Solution
3.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control get nodes. Then kube control dash n cord describe pod dash l app queue then pipe to grep dash i -A two Failed Scheduling then pipe to head -four. Then kube control uncordon C K A worker C K A worker two. Then kube control dash n cord rollout status deployment queue the timeout flag set to one hundred twenty seconds. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

3.title: Recall Check 1
3.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. A node is Not Ready. Which two services do you check first? Answer: kubelet and container D ( system control status, journal control dash u kubelet ). Question two. kube control is refused. Which tool inspects the A P I server container? Answer: C R I C T L ps dash a and C R I C T L logs on the control plane node. Question three. Where do you fix a broken control plane component? Answer: In its static Pod manifest in slash E T C slash Kubernetes slash manifests or; the kubelet restarts it.

3.title: Recall Check 2
3.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. New Pods stay Pending with no node assigned and existing Pods are fine. Which component? Answer: The scheduler. Question five. A Deployment shows no Replica Set. Which component? Answer: The controller manager. Question six. What does Scheduling Disabled mean and how do you undo it? Answer: The node is cordoned; kube control uncordon node.

3.title: Recall Check 3
3.text: Recall check three. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question seven. What does "connection refused" tell you about the A P I server address? Answer: Nothing is listening there: wrong server in the kube config or the A P I server is down. Question eight. What is the difference between system control start kubelet and system control enable the now flag kubelet? Answer: start runs it now; enable the now flag also starts it at every boot.

3.title: Module Recap
3.text: Here is the recap. Node Not Ready: kubelet, container D, journal control dash u kubelet, C N I. Kubelet files: slash var slash lib slash kubelet slash config dot yaml, slash E T C slash Kubernetes slash kubelet dot conf, system control cat kubelet. Control plane fix: edit the manifest in slash E T C slash Kubernetes slash manifests or; kubelet restarts it. A P I server down: C R I C T L ps dash a, C R I C T L logs, check E T C D flags and cert paths. Symptoms: Pending no node equals scheduler; no Replica Set equals controller manager; refused equals A P I server or kube config. Cordoned: Scheduling Disabled - greater than uncordon. Always: back up the manifest, fix the root cause, verify the original symptom. In the next module, we continue the course.
